stated: Fairly reform capital gains tax to close loopholes currently exploited by the super wealthy, aiming to raise money for investment plans.

source.quote: Fairly reforming capital gains tax to close loopholes exploited by the super wealthy.

bearing_set.reason: CGT loophole closure directly affects returns on business investment and entrepreneurship; contested evidence on whether higher effective rates dampen capital formation, investment levels, and job creation or merely realign incentives — a non-negligible verdict on work and pay quality.
Closing CGT loopholes raises the effective tax burden on capital gains for those currently exploiting them, directly worsening O11 for the affected group (the super-wealthy).
The explicit aim is to raise revenue earmarked for investment plans; if successful this improves the funded vs. borrowed balance, bearing materially on debt sustainability.

CGT reform reshapes investment incentives and capital allocation decisions (closing loopholes can reduce distortionary tax-motivated activity while funded investment plans could lift long-run productivity) — both near-term and long-term effects on prosperity are non-negligible.

The policy explicitly targets loopholes used by the super-wealthy; closing them narrows the effective-tax-rate gap between capital owners and wage earners, bearing directly on the income/wealth inequality gap.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear on this policy: a direct tax-burden effect (O11), a revenue/fiscal effect (O12), an investment-incentive and productivity effect (O13), and an inequality-narrowing effect (O14). O9/O10 do not apply (no discrimination or liberty mechanism). O2/O3 are at most incidental — how investment proceeds are spent is unspecified.
